newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close weaker, Jospin speech awaited.
newsitem.headline: French shares close weaker, Jospin speech awaited.

text.p: French shares closed weaker after a day of light trading on Wednesday amid investor caution ahead of Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's debut parliamentary policy speech on Thursday.

The CAC-40 blue-chip index ended down 0.39 percent, or 10.86 points, at 2,751, after shedding more than one percent earlier in the day. The CAC-40 futures contract finished three points down at 2,748.
Analysts say it is unclear whether Jospin can elaborate significantly on economic policy and privatisations after two weeks in government and ahead of an audit of state finances.

Jospin is due to make his speech to the National Assembly from 1500 GMT under pressure to deliver on promises that jobs and work time cuts take priority over austerity and amid demands to raise the minimum wage and reopen talks on public sector pay.
*LVMH shares ended 1.7 percent lower, recovering somewhat from hefty opening losses after announcing on Tuesday it had bought 0.23 percent of Grand Metropolitan GMET.PA.

It says it is not planning to make an offer and declined to elaborate on Wednesday. Analysts believe it it manoeuvering to defend its drinks links with Guinness after Guinness and Grand Met's recent merger announcement.

* Appliance maker Moulinex reported a 1996/97 net attributable profit of 29 million francs, its first full-year profit since 1991. It had a 702 million franc loss in 1995/96 after taking a 600 million restructuring charge.
It said it expected a significant rise in operating profit and return on capital for the 1997/98 year after an increase in operating profit to 160 million from 54 million in 1996/97.
* Stock market volume was 7.1 billion francs.

* Skis Rossignol closed sharply up despite a 34.2 percent drop in 1996/97 profit to 76.1 million francs. Investors responded well to a relatively robust operating profit and saw provisions as a sign of a clean-up, fund managers said.
* Credit Lyonnais state-onwed bank investment certificates major gainer, closing up 6.99 percent. Leven brokerage cited as switching to buy recommendation on the non-voting stock.
* Oil group Total, industrial Alcatel and electronics group Schneider end weaker, with share dips attributed by traders to profit-taking.
